Timer Expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

So this is a pretty neat article with a very tight knit story contained within, in which we watch an article evolve over time with new developments. With how tight knit this story is, the best kind of link would be an inline edit that doesn't seriously disturb the narrative flow. Such a link could be made, as LurkD pointed out when I consulted them via PM, to the Site-45 dossier, which would allow a reader to not only find out more about the site that is a big part of this article, but also all the other objects mentioned in that hub. As such, I am proposing the following edits:

This (found in "REVISION" tab):

SCP-466 is to be sealed in Containment Cell-73 in E-Block at Research Site-45. E-Block is to remain separated from the main installation for the entirety of SCP-466's captivity. Containment Cell-73 is to have a 30cm thick acrylic observational window installed and the door welded shut from the outside.

Be changed to this:

SCP-466 is to be sealed in Containment Cell-73 in E-Block at Research Site-45. E-Block is to remain separated from the main installation for the entirety of SCP-466's captivity. Containment Cell-73 is to have a 30cm thick acrylic observational window installed and the door welded shut from the outside.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Found this through a comment left in the March Madness Deathmatch forum, of all places, and I have to say this is amazing, and one of the more enjoyable and interesting skips I've read in a while. It's body horror done well, it succeeds at being scary because it focuses on a story, not on shock value. I especially liked the interview logs. I was surprised at how well it was written for an older article, until I saw it was a rewrite - makes sense (incidentally, the weakest part of the article for me was the tab with the original skip).

A few nitpicks:
A few nitpicks:

I personally liked the blood test log because it adds realism, even though I understood nothing of it (at least it was color-coded, though, so at least I could tell which of those things I know nothing about wasn't within normal levels). I suggest adding a few lines at the bottom where a doctor comments on what was discovered, explaining the anomalous readings in layman's terms. It would make sense to have that there, since not all Foundation personnel reading the fie will have a medical background.

Another thing: maybe I wasn't paying enough attention, but the description of the creature after the autopsy incident felt really vague (for example, does it still have a body? i suggest stating this more implicitly). Also, calling the human part of the creature "466-2" in earlier tabs, then suddenly referring to it as "the patient" post-incident really confused me, for a while I thought there was another person involved.

Agent Foster: Alright, than- (ahem)

pretty sure that should be "Allright, then"

to the respective brain stem

"respective" isn't necessary IMO, since there's only one brain stem, not several.

SCP-466 is able to oxygenate without the use of lungs. It is theorized to extract it from the surrounding air.

to extract what? you only say "oxygenate" in the first sentence, not "oxygen".

This is the same for the absorption of nutrients as well.

redundant
Congratulations - an absolute cracker of a horror concept, one of the best re-writes I can recall seeing, and great immersive use of the format screw.

This is definitely on my list of favorite articles now.

item.content:encoded:
Very cool.

A couple of tiny issues:

Agent Foster: Right… no lungs. Blink once for yes, twice for no. Alright?
Patient: (blink)
Agent Foster: Good. Um… is your name [REDACTED] and you are ██ years old?

I would think an agent would understand that you can't ask two questions in the same sentence like that when the respondent can only say yes or no. He would ask one at a time. Otherwise, the answer could be yes to one part and no to the other, and it would be impossible for the respondent to adequately express that.

In lieu of the situation regarding SCP-466, whereas the current containment procedures no longer apply to its current condition and thereby necessitate the review and development of more applicable procedures and containment protocols, the following draft has been proposed.

I think you might mean "In light of" (unless I've misunderstood).

That aside, I loved it.
